name: Storm over Riverlands
description: Entity Water's river simulation set into Entity Cloud's High Plains: the clouds, rain shafts, haze and lightning are drawn over the river world, and rain falling where the camera is turns on the river's rain.

name: Imposter Valley weather
description: Entity Imposter's valley (15k trees, rocks and homesteads as octahedral imposters) out on Entity Cloud's High Plains: its forests under volumetric clouds, storm shafts and lightning, lit by the plains' sun.

name: Bunker on the Reservoir
description: Entity Portal's bunker compound (portal-room visibility, stencil-masked traversal, a freighter, drones) as an island in Entity Cloud's Reservoir: walk out of the bunker into the plains' weather. Indoors (a portal area that isn't the outdoors) the rain stays outside.

name: Planetfall
description: Entity Imposter's valley set on Entity Origin's real-scale Earth: one floating-origin camera flies from the valley floor up to Gateway Station in orbit and on to Neptune, the valley staying exact under it. The valley's sun is the solar system's.

name: Sector 07 on the Moon
description: Entity GUI's facility (airlock terminal, CCTV, easel, handheld) stands at Entity Origin's Shackleton Base on the Moon. Fly around it with the floating-origin camera; ` hands the keys and the camera to the facility's player inside, with its world-space GUIs.

name: Grand tour of the plains
description: Four engines in one world: Entity Cloud's High Plains as the sky over Entity Water's Riverlands, Entity Imposter's valley and Entity Portal's bunker island, flown with the engine's free camera. Untick a world in the bar to see the others without it.

name: Oʻahu
description: The island of Oʻahu at 1:1: its real ground (AWS Terrain Tiles, 36 m cells, cut to OpenStreetMap's coastline), its 6,800 km of mapped roads with rounded curves, bridges and US markings, and its 97,000 mapped buildings stood up from their footprints, under trade-wind weather. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL); made by tools/geo-import.mjs.

name: GUI depth stress
description: EntityGUI screens at 2 m to 512 m, one per view: how deep a world-space GUI can be before it breaks.

name: GUI swarm stress
description: 296 world-space EntityGUIs at once: a ring of terminals, a 72-panel video wall, 144 hovering panels at every angle, a stack of overlapping screens, giants up to 25 m wide and 24 easels with their own paint targets, on every terminal page, CRT and flat. More GUIs than the 8-bit stencil has values: the rest fall back to the depth test.
